# Pueue

![Pueue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nukesor/images/main/pueue-v2.0.0.gif)

Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks.

Simply put, it's a tool that **p**rocesses a q**ueue** of shell commands.
On top of that, there are a lot of convenient features and abstractions.

Since Pueue is not bound to any terminal, you can control your tasks from any terminal on the same machine.
The queue will be continuously processed, even if you no longer have any active ssh sessions.

## Features

- Scheduling
  - Add tasks as you go.
  - Run multiple tasks at once. You decide how many tasks should run concurrently.
  - Change the order of the scheduled tasks.
  - Specify dependencies between tasks.
  - Schedule tasks to run at a specific time.
- Process interaction
  - Easy output inspection.
  - Send input to running processes.
  - Pause/resume tasks, when you need some processing power right NOW!
- Task groups (multiple queues)
  - Each group can have several tasks running in parallel.
  - Pause/start tasks by a group.
- Background process execution
  - The `pueued` daemon runs in the background. No need to be logged in.
  - Commands are executed in their respective working directories.
  - The current environment variables are copied when adding a task.
  - Commands are run in a shell which allows the full feature set of shell coding.
- Consistency
  - The queue is always saved to disk and restored on kill/system crash.
  - Logs are persisted onto the disk and survive a crash.
- Miscellaneous
  - A callback hook to, for instance, set up desktop notifications.
  - JSON output for `log` and `status` if you want to display info about tasks in another program.
  - A `wait` subcommand to wait for specific tasks, a group (or everything) to finish.
- A lot more. Check the -h options for each subcommand for detailed options.
- Cross Platform
  - Linux is fully supported and battle-tested.
  - MacOS is fully supported and on par with Linux.
  - Windows is fully supported and working fine for quite a while.

## What Pueue is **not**

Pueue is **not** designed to be a heavy-duty programmable (scriptable) task scheduler/executor.

The focus of `pueue` lies on human interaction, i.e. it's supposed to be used by a real person on some kind of OS.

Due to this, the feature set of `pueue` and `pueued` as well as their implementation and architecture have been kept simple by design!
Even though it can be scripted to some degree, it hasn't been built for heavy-duty work like hundreds of tasks!

## Installation

Pueue can be installed via your system's package manager, or by downloading prebuilt binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/releases).

## How to Use it

Pueue consists of two components:
- `pueued` - The daemon that runs in the background and manages your tasks
- `pueue` - The client used to interact with the daemon

### Basic Commands

```text
Interact with the Pueue daemon

Usage: pueue [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add            Enqueue a task for execution.
                     There're many different options when scheduling a task.
                     Check the individual option help texts for more information.

                     Furthermore, please remember that scheduled commands are executed via your system shell.
                     This means that the command needs proper shell escaping.
                     The safest way to preserve shell escaping is to surround your command with quotes, for example:
                     pueue add 'ls $HOME && echo "Some string"'
  remove         Remove tasks from the list. Running or paused tasks need to be killed first
  switch         Switches the queue position of two commands. Only works on queued and stashed commands
  stash          Stashed tasks won't be automatically started. You have to enqueue them or start them by hand
  enqueue        Enqueue stashed tasks. They'll be handled normally afterwards
  start          Resume operation of specific tasks or groups of tasks.
                     By default, this resumes the default group and all its tasks.
                     Can also be used force-start specific tasks.
  restart        Restart failed or successful task(s).
                     By default, identical tasks will be created and enqueued, but it's possible to restart in-place.
                     You can also edit a few properties, such as the path and the command, before restarting.
  pause          Either pause running tasks or specific groups of tasks.
                     By default, pauses the default group and all its tasks.
                     A paused queue (group) won't start any new tasks.
  kill           Kill specific running tasks or whole task groups..
                     Kills all tasks of the default group when no ids or a specific group are provided.
  send           Send something to a task. Useful for sending confirmations such as 'y\n'

## Similar Projects

#### slurm

[Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/overview.html) is a feature rich and widely used cluster management and scheduling system.
If you find yourself in the need for complex setups such as multiple worker pools or distributed nodes, slurm will be much better suited than Pueue.

#### GNU Parallel

A robust and featureful parallel processor with text-based joblog and n-retries. [GNU Parallel](https://www.gnu.org/software/parallel/parallel_tutorial.html) is able to scale to multi-host parallelization and has complex code to have deep integration across different tools and shells, as well as other advanced features. `Pueue` differentiates itself from GNU Parallel by focusing more on visibility across many different long running commands, and creating a central location for commands to be stored, rather than GNU Parallel's focus on chunking a specific task.

#### Pm2

[pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/quick-start/) is a process management tool, whose focus is more on management of recurring and long-living tasks.
It seems to be quite mature and has a rich interface.

#### nq

A very lightweight job queue system which advertises no setup, maintenance, supervision, or otherwise long-running background processes. \
[Link to project](https://github.com/leahneukirchen/nq)

#### task-spooler

_task spooler_ is a Unix batch system where the tasks spooled run one after the other. \
Links to [ubuntu manpage](http://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/xenial/man1/tsp.1.html) and a [fork on Github](https://github.com/xenogenesi/task-spooler).

## Similar Projects

#### slurm

[Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/overview.html) is a feature rich and widely used cluster management and scheduling system.
If you find yourself in the need for complex setups such as multiple worker pools or distributed nodes, slurm will be much better suited than Pueue.

#### GNU Parallel

A robust and featureful parallel processor with text-based joblog and n-retries. [GNU Parallel](https://www.gnu.org/software/parallel/parallel_tutorial.html) is able to scale to multi-host parallelization and has complex code to have deep integration across different tools and shells, as well as other advanced features. `Pueue` differentiates itself from GNU Parallel by focusing more on visibility across many different long running commands, and creating a central location for commands to be stored, rather than GNU Parallel's focus on chunking a specific task.

#### Pm2

[pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/quick-start/) is a process management tool, whose focus is more on management of recurring and long-living tasks.
It seems to be quite mature and has a rich interface.

#### nq

A very lightweight job queue system which advertises no setup, maintenance, supervision, or otherwise long-running background processes. \
[Link to project](https://github.com/leahneukirchen/nq)

#### task-spooler

_task spooler_ is a Unix batch system where the tasks spooled run one after the other. \

	string join \n v/verbose color= c/config= p/profile= h/help V/version

"""Rendering of help paragraphs and aligned command-line reference tables."""
import os
import re
import textwrap
from help_text import HELP_TEXT


def wrap_words(text, width):
    # Words and existing newlines are meaningful, but long words are never split.
    if not text:
        return ['']
    return textwrap.wrap(text, max(width, 1), expand_tabs=False,
                         replace_whitespace=False, break_long_words=False,
                         break_on_hyphens=False, drop_whitespace=True) or ['']


def render_help(name, long, program, width=None):
    if name.endswith('help'):
        return ('Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)\n\n'
                f'Usage: {program} {name} [COMMAND]...\n\n'
                'Arguments:\n'
                '  [COMMAND]...  Print help for the subcommand(s)\n')
    source = HELP_TEXT[name]['long' if long else 'short']
    source = source.replace('Usage: executable', 'Usage: ' + program)
    if width is None:
        try:
            width = int(os.environ.get('COLUMNS', '100'))
        except ValueError:
            width = 100
    if width == 0:
        width = 1000000
    result = []
    table = ''
    cell_indent = 0
    lines = source.splitlines()
    # Compact tables are padded as a whole, even for narrower terminals.
    section_indents = {}
    sec = ''
    for line in lines:
        if line in ('Options:', 'Arguments:', 'Commands:'):
            sec = line
        m = re.match(r'^(  \S.*?)( {2,})(\S.*)$', line)
        if m and (line.lstrip().startswith(('-', '<', '[')) or sec == 'Commands:'):
            section_indents[sec] = max(section_indents.get(sec, 0), len(m[1])+len(m[2]))
    for line in lines:
        if not line:
            result.append('')
            continue
        if line in ('Options:', 'Arguments:', 'Commands:'):
            table = line
            result.append(line)
            continue
        if line.startswith('Usage:'):
            result.append(line)
            continue
        if table and not line.startswith(' '):
            table = ''
        m = re.match(r'^(  \S.*?)( {2,})(\S.*)$', line)
        if table and m and (line.lstrip().startswith(('-', '<', '[')) or table == 'Commands:'):
            prefix = m[1] + m[2]
            cell_indent = section_indents[table]
            # Continuation lines of compact option descriptions have one extra
            # pad column if an option has a value rather than being a switch.
            chunks = wrap_words(m[3], width-cell_indent)
            result.append(prefix + chunks[0])
            result.extend(' ' * cell_indent + c for c in chunks[1:])
        elif table and line.lstrip().startswith(('-', '<', '[')) and len(line)-len(line.lstrip()) < 8:
            result.append(line)
        else:
            if not line.strip():
                result.append(line)
                continue
            n = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(' '))
            chunks = wrap_words(line[n:], width-n)
            result += [' ' * n + c for c in chunks]
    return '\n'.join(result) + '\n'

@dataclass
class Command:

    positionals: list = field(default_factory=list)
    children: list = field(default_factory=list)
    child_required: bool = False
    trailing: bool = False

    def find_option(self, spelling):
        for opt in self.options:

        return None

        items = [program]

        if any(o.long not in ('help', 'version') for o in self.options):

        items += [p.display(p.required) for p in self.positionals]

"""Rendering of help paragraphs and aligned command-line reference tables."""
import os
import re
import textwrap
from help_text import HELP_TEXT


def wrap_words(text, width):
    # Words and existing newlines are meaningful, but long words are never split.
    if not text:
        return ['']
    return textwrap.wrap(text, max(width, 1), expand_tabs=False,
                         replace_whitespace=False, break_long_words=False,
                         break_on_hyphens=False, drop_whitespace=True) or ['']


def render_help(name, long, program, width=None):
    if name.endswith('help'):
        return ('Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)\n\n'
                f'Usage: {program} {name} [COMMAND]...\n\n'
                'Arguments:\n'
                '  [COMMAND]...  Print help for the subcommand(s)\n')
    source = HELP_TEXT[name]['long' if long else 'short']
    source = source.replace('Usage: executable', 'Usage: ' + program)
    if width is None:
        try:
            width = int(os.environ.get('COLUMNS', '100'))
        except ValueError:
            width = 100
    if width == 0:
        width = 1000000
    result = []
    table = ''
    cell_indent = 0
    lines = source.splitlines()
    # Compact tables are padded as a whole, even for narrower terminals.
    section_indents = {}
    sec = ''
    for line in lines:
        if line in ('Options:', 'Arguments:', 'Commands:'):
            sec = line
        m = re.match(r'^(  \S.*?)( {2,})(\S.*)$', line)
        if m and (line.lstrip().startswith(('-', '<', '[')) or sec == 'Commands:'):
            section_indents[sec] = max(section_indents.get(sec, 0), len(m[1])+len(m[2]))
    for line in lines:
        if not line:
            result.append('')
            continue
        if line in ('Options:', 'Arguments:', 'Commands:'):
            table = line
            result.append(line)
            continue
        if line.startswith('Usage:'):
            result.append(line)
            continue
        if table and not line.startswith(' '):
            table = ''
        m = re.match(r'^(  \S.*?)( {2,})(\S.*)$', line)
        if table and m and (line.lstrip().startswith(('-', '<', '[')) or table == 'Commands:'):
            prefix = m[1] + m[2]
            cell_indent = section_indents[table]
            # Continuation lines of compact option descriptions have one extra
            # pad column if an option has a value rather than being a switch.
            chunks = wrap_words(m[3], width-cell_indent)
            result.append(prefix + chunks[0])
            result.extend(' ' * cell_indent + c for c in chunks[1:])
        elif table and line.lstrip().startswith(('-', '<', '[')) and len(line)-len(line.lstrip()) < 8:
            result.append(line)
        else:
            if not line.strip():
                result.append(line)
                continue
            n = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(' '))
            chunks = wrap_words(line[n:], width-n)
            result += [' ' * n + c for c in chunks]
    return '\n'.join(result) + '\n'

RESET='\x1b[0m'

def paint(text,style):return style+text+RESET

    if match:

    return paint('Usage:',HEADER)+' '+tail

    if not enabled(stream or sys.stdout):return text

        elif line in ('Commands:','Options:','Arguments:'):
            section=line

        elif not line.startswith(' ') and line:
            section=''

            line=re.sub(r'^(  )(\S+)',lambda m:m[1]+paint(m[2],BOLD),line)
        elif section=='Options:' and re.match(r'^ {2,6}-',line):
            # Only the option declaration is styled, not examples in its help.
            m=re.match(r'^( {2,6}-.*?)( {2,}\S.*)?$',line)
            label=m[1] if m else line
            rest=m[2] or '' if m else ''
            label=re.sub(r'(?<![\w-])(--?[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*)',lambda m:paint(m[1],BOLD),label)
            line=label+rest

    if not enabled(sys.stderr):return text

    missing=False;conflicts=False

            missing=msg.startswith('the following required arguments')
            conflicts=msg.endswith('cannot be used with:')
            if msg.startswith(('invalid value ', 'unexpected value ')):

            line=paint('error:',RED)+' '+msg
        elif line.startswith('Usage: '):line=usage(line)
        elif line.startswith('For more information, try '):line=line.replace("'--help'","'"+paint('--help',BOLD)+"'")
        elif line.startswith('  [possible values: '):
            vals=line[len('  [possible values: '):-1].split(', ')

                for i,s in enumerate(pieces):

        elif line.startswith('  ') and (missing or conflicts):
            line='  '+paint(line[2:],GREEN if missing else YELLOW)
        result.append(line)

"""Black-box regression tests for the independently built executable."""
import hashlib
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
EXECUTABLE=ROOT/'executable'


class CommandLineTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp=tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.base=Path(self.temp.name)
        self.cwd=self.base/'cwd'
        self.cwd.mkdir()
        self.env={k:v for k,v in os.environ.items() if k not in (
            'PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH','RUST_LOG','RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE','CLICOLOR_FORCE','NO_COLOR','CLICOLOR')}
        self.env.update(HOME=str(self.base/'home'),XDG_CONFIG_HOME=str(self.base/'config'),
                        XDG_DATA_HOME=str(self.base/'data'),XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=str(self.base/'runtime'),
                        COLUMNS='100',TERM='dumb',RUST_BACKTRACE='0')

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def call(self,*args,env=None):
        return subprocess.run([str(EXECUTABLE),*args],input=b'',capture_output=True,
                              cwd=self.cwd,env={**self.env,**(env or {})},timeout=5)

    def config(self,text):
        path=self.base/'config.yml'
        path.write_text(text)
        return str(path)

    def assertNoConfig(self,*args):
        result=self.call(*args)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1,result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'')
        self.assertIn(b"Couldn't find a configuration file. Did you start the daemon yet?",result.stderr)
        return result

    def test_version(self):
        for flag in ('-V','--version'):
            p=self.call(flag)
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,b'pueue 4.0.4\n',b''))

    def test_main_help(self):
        p=self.call('--help')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,b'')
        self.assertIn(b'Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]\n',p.stdout)
        self.assertIn(b'  completions  Generates shell completion files\n',p.stdout)
        self.assertNotEqual(self.call('-h').stdout,p.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('help').stdout,p.stdout)

    def test_all_command_help(self):
        names=['add','remove','switch','stash','enqueue','start','restart','pause','kill',
               'send','edit','env','group','status','log','follow','wait','clean','reset',
               'shutdown','parallel','completions']
        for name in names:
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                p=self.call(name,'--help')
                self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stderr),(0,b''))
                self.assertIn(('Usage: executable '+name).encode(),p.stdout)

    def test_nested_help_and_aliases(self):
        for args in [('env','set'),('env','unset'),('group','add'),('group','remove')]:
            self.assertEqual(self.call(*args,'--help').stdout,self.call('help',*args).stdout)
        for alias,canonical in [('rm','remove'),('re','restart'),('fo','follow'),('clear','clean'),('cleanup','clean')]:
            self.assertEqual(self.call(alias,'--help').stdout,self.call(canonical,'--help').stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('env').returncode,2)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('env').stderr,self.call('env','--help').stdout)

    def test_no_configuration(self):
        for args in [(),('status',),('add','echo hello'),('group',),('parallel','0'),('reset','--force')]:
            self.assertNoConfig(*args)

    def test_missing_required(self):
        p=self.call('add')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,2)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,b"error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <COMMAND>...\n\nUsage: executable add <COMMAND>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        self.assertIn(b'<TASK_ID_2>',self.call('switch','1').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'<VALUE>',self.call('env','set','1','KEY').stderr)

    def test_integer_validation(self):
        self.assertNoConfig('remove','18446744073709551615')
        self.assertIn(b'number too large to fit in target type',self.call('remove','18446744073709551616').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'for \'[TASK_IDS]...\'',self.call('start','oops').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"unexpected argument '-1'",self.call('remove','-1').stderr)
        self.assertNoConfig('add','--priority=-1','echo')
        self.assertIn(b'not in -2147483648..=2147483647',self.call('add','--priority=2147483648','echo').stderr)

    def test_deferred_values_and_trailing_command(self):
        self.assertNoConfig('add','echo','--help')
        self.assertNoConfig('add','--after=1','echo')
        self.assertIn(b"invalid value 'echo' for '--after",self.call('add','--after','1','echo').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"unexpected argument '--bad'",self.call('remove','bad','--bad').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"invalid value 'bad'",self.call('remove','bad','--help').stderr)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('--color','invalid','status','--help').returncode,0)

    def test_conflicts(self):
        for args,left,right in [
            (('add','-i','-s','echo'),b'--immediate',b'--stashed'),
            (('start','-g','test','-a'),b'--group <GROUP>',b'--all'),
            (('log','-l','3','-f'),b'--lines <LINES>',b'--full')]:
            p=self.call(*args)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode,2)
            self.assertIn(b"the argument '"+left+b"' cannot be used with '"+right+b"'",p.stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'--immediate',self.call('add','--follow','echo').stderr)
        self.assertNoConfig('add','--stashed','--follow','echo')

    def test_enumerations(self):
        for status in ('queued','Queued','running','Running','done','Done','success','Success'):
            self.assertNoConfig('wait','-s',status)
        for status in ('failed','stashed','paused','QUEUED'):
            self.assertEqual(self.call('wait','-s',status).returncode,2)
        for signal in ('SIGINT','term','stop','cont','9','2'):
            self.assertNoConfig('kill','-s',signal)
        for signal in ('0','SIGHUP','usr1','sig2'):
            self.assertEqual(self.call('kill','-s',signal).returncode,2)

    def test_delay_syntax(self):
        for delay in ('60','tomorrow','-1','2h','1d 03:00','2027-04-01T18:30:00','25:00','1 apr 2027','0.5'):
            self.assertNoConfig('enqueue','--delay='+delay)
        for delay in ('nonsense','10ms','1.60','2h30m','in 2 hours','April 1 2020 18:30:00','9223372036854775807'):
            self.assertIn(b'could not parse as seconds or date expression',self.call('enqueue','--delay='+delay).stderr)

    def test_suggestions(self):
        self.assertIn(b"a similar subcommand exists: 'completions'",self.call('completion').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"a similar argument exists: '--json'",self.call('status','--jsoon').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"'status --json' exists",self.call('--json','status').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"a similar value exists: 'power-shell'",self.call('completions','powershell').stderr)

    def test_configuration_paths(self):
        path=self.base/'not-present.yml'
        p=self.call('--config',str(path))
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(('I/O error at path "'+str(path)+'" while opening config file').encode(),p.stderr)
        p=self.call('-c',self.config('{}\n'))
        self.assertIn((str(self.base/'data/pueue/shared_secret')).encode(),p.stderr)
        self.assertFalse((self.base/'data/pueue').exists())

    def test_configuration_environment_override(self):
        bad=str(self.base/'missing-env.yml')
        self.assertIn(b'missing-env.yml',self.call(env={'PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH':bad}).stderr)
        p=self.call('-c',self.config('shared:\n  pueue_directory: custom-data\n'),env={'PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH':bad})
        self.assertIn(b'custom-data/shared_secret',p.stderr)
        self.assertNotIn(b'missing-env.yml',p.stderr)

    def test_config_search_priority(self):
        home_config=self.base/'config/pueue/pueue.yml'
        home_config.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        home_config.write_text('shared:\n  pueue_directory: first\n')
        (self.cwd/'pueue.yml').write_text('shared:\n  pueue_directory: second\n')
        self.assertIn(b'"first/shared_secret"',self.call().stderr)
        home_config.unlink()
        self.assertIn(b'"second/shared_secret"',self.call().stderr)

    def test_profiles_are_independent(self):
        path=self.config('shared:\n  pueue_directory: base-data\nprofiles:\n  empty: {}\n  work:\n    shared:\n      pueue_directory: profile-data\n')
        self.assertIn(b'base-data/shared_secret',self.call('-c',path).stderr)
        self.assertIn(str(self.base/'data/pueue/shared_secret').encode(),self.call('-c',path,'-p','empty').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'profile-data/shared_secret',self.call('-c',path,'-p','work').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'Couldn\'t find profile with name "absent"',self.call('-c',path,'-p','absent').stderr)

    def test_yaml_validation(self):
        path=self.config('shared:\n  use_unix_socket: "yes"\n')
        self.assertIn(b'shared.use_unix_socket: invalid type: string "yes", expected a boolean at line 2 column 20',self.call('-c',path).stderr)
        path=self.config('client: {}\nclient: {}\n')
        self.assertIn(b'duplicate field `client`',self.call('-c',path).stderr)
        path=self.config('shared:\n  use_unix_socket: [\n')
        self.assertIn(b'invalid type: sequence, expected a boolean',self.call('-c',path).stderr)
        path=self.config('profiles:\ndaemon:\n  env_vars: {unset_me: null}\n')
        self.assertNotIn(b'Failed to read configuration.',self.call('-c',path).stderr)

        secret=self.base/'secret'
        secret.write_bytes(b'example secret')
        socket=self.base/'missing.socket'
        path=self.config(f'shared:\n  shared_secret_path: {secret}\n  unix_socket_path: {socket}\n')
        result=self.call('-c',path,'status')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)

        self.assertIn(b'while connecting to daemon. Did you start it?',result.stderr)
        self.assertIn(str(socket).encode(),result.stderr)

        p=self.call('remove','bad',env={'CLICOLOR_FORCE':'1'})
        self.assertTrue(p.stderr.startswith(b'\x1b[1m\x1b[31merror:'))
        p=self.call('remove','bad',env={'CLICOLOR_FORCE':'1','NO_COLOR':'1'})
        self.assertNotIn(b'\x1b',p.stderr)
        p=self.call('--color','always','--help')
        self.assertNotIn(b'\x1b',p.stdout)
        # Runtime diagnostic rendering is independent of the table-color policy.
        self.assertIn(b'\x1b[91m',self.assertNoConfig('--color','never').stderr)

    def test_completion_files(self):
        names={'bash':'pueue.bash','elvish':'pueue.elv','fish':'pueue.fish',
               'power-shell':'_pueue.ps1','zsh':'_pueue','nushell':'pueue.nu'}
        for shell,filename in names.items():

        p=self.call('completions','bash',str(self.base/'missing/destination'))
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(b'Failed to generate completions for Bash',p.stderr)


# Golden digests of the shell completion text observed through the CLI.
COMPLETION_HASHES = {}

if __name__=='__main__':
    unittest.main()

        self.assertIn(b'Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]\n',p.stdout)
        self.assertIn(b'  completions  Generates shell completion files\n',p.stdout)
        self.assertNotEqual(self.call('-h').stdout,p.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('help').stdout,p.stdout)

    def test_all_command_help(self):
        names=['add','remove','switch','stash','enqueue','start','restart','pause','kill',
               'send','edit','env','group','status','log','follow','wait','clean','reset',
               'shutdown','parallel','completions']
        for name in names:
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                p=self.call(name,'--help')
                self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stderr),(0,b''))
                self.assertIn(('Usage: executable '+name).encode(),p.stdout)

    def test_nested_help_and_aliases(self):
        for args in [('env','set'),('env','unset'),('group','add'),('group','remove')]:
            self.assertEqual(self.call(*args,'--help').stdout,self.call('help',*args).stdout)
        for alias,canonical in [('rm','remove'),('re','restart'),('fo','follow'),('clear','clean'),('cleanup','clean')]:
            self.assertEqual(self.call(alias,'--help').stdout,self.call(canonical,'--help').stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('env').returncode,2)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('env').stderr,self.call('env','--help').stdout)

    def test_no_configuration(self):
        for args in [(),('status',),('add','echo hello'),('group',),('parallel','0'),('reset','--force')]:
            self.assertNoConfig(*args)

    def test_missing_required(self):
        p=self.call('add')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,2)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,b"error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <COMMAND>...\n\nUsage: executable add <COMMAND>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        self.assertIn(b'<TASK_ID_2>',self.call('switch','1').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'<VALUE>',self.call('env','set','1','KEY').stderr)

    def test_integer_validation(self):
        self.assertNoConfig('remove','18446744073709551615')
        self.assertIn(b'number too large to fit in target type',self.call('remove','18446744073709551616').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'for \'[TASK_IDS]...\'',self.call('start','oops').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"unexpected argument '-1'",self.call('remove','-1').stderr)
        self.assertNoConfig('add','--priority=-1','echo')
        self.assertIn(b'not in -2147483648..=2147483647',self.call('add','--priority=2147483648','echo').stderr)

    def test_deferred_values_and_trailing_command(self):
        self.assertNoConfig('add','echo','--help')
        self.assertNoConfig('add','--after=1','echo')
        self.assertIn(b"invalid value 'echo' for '--after",self.call('add','--after','1','echo').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"unexpected argument '--bad'",self.call('remove','bad','--bad').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"invalid value 'bad'",self.call('remove','bad','--help').stderr)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('--color','invalid','status','--help').returncode,0)

    def test_conflicts(self):
        for args,left,right in [
            (('add','-i','-s','echo'),b'--immediate',b'--stashed'),
            (('start','-g','test','-a'),b'--group <GROUP>',b'--all'),
            (('log','-l','3','-f'),b'--lines <LINES>',b'--full')]:
            p=self.call(*args)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode,2)
            self.assertIn(b"the argument '"+left+b"' cannot be used with '"+right+b"'",p.stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'--immediate',self.call('add','--follow','echo').stderr)
        self.assertNoConfig('add','--stashed','--follow','echo')

    def test_enumerations(self):
        for status in ('queued','Queued','running','Running','done','Done','success','Success'):
            self.assertNoConfig('wait','-s',status)
        for status in ('failed','stashed','paused','QUEUED'):
            self.assertEqual(self.call('wait','-s',status).returncode,2)
        for signal in ('SIGINT','term','stop','cont','9','2'):
            self.assertNoConfig('kill','-s',signal)
        for signal in ('0','SIGHUP','usr1','sig2'):
            self.assertEqual(self.call('kill','-s',signal).returncode,2)

    def test_delay_syntax(self):
        for delay in ('60','tomorrow','-1','2h','1d 03:00','2027-04-01T18:30:00','25:00','1 apr 2027','0.5'):
            self.assertNoConfig('enqueue','--delay='+delay)
        for delay in ('nonsense','10ms','1.60','2h30m','in 2 hours','April 1 2020 18:30:00','9223372036854775807'):
            self.assertIn(b'could not parse as seconds or date expression',self.call('enqueue','--delay='+delay).stderr)

    def test_suggestions(self):
        self.assertIn(b"a similar subcommand exists: 'completions'",self.call('completion').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"a similar argument exists: '--json'",self.call('status','--jsoon').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"'status --json' exists",self.call('--json','status').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b"a similar value exists: 'power-shell'",self.call('completions','powershell').stderr)

    def test_configuration_paths(self):
        path=self.base/'not-present.yml'
        p=self.call('--config',str(path))
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(('I/O error at path "'+str(path)+'" while opening config file').encode(),p.stderr)
        p=self.call('-c',self.config('{}\n'))
        self.assertIn((str(self.base/'data/pueue/shared_secret')).encode(),p.stderr)
        self.assertFalse((self.base/'data/pueue').exists())

    def test_configuration_environment_override(self):
        bad=str(self.base/'missing-env.yml')
        self.assertIn(b'missing-env.yml',self.call(env={'PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH':bad}).stderr)
        p=self.call('-c',self.config('shared:\n  pueue_directory: custom-data\n'),env={'PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH':bad})
        self.assertIn(b'custom-data/shared_secret',p.stderr)
        self.assertNotIn(b'missing-env.yml',p.stderr)

    def test_config_search_priority(self):
        home_config=self.base/'config/pueue/pueue.yml'
        home_config.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        home_config.write_text('shared:\n  pueue_directory: first\n')
        (self.cwd/'pueue.yml').write_text('shared:\n  pueue_directory: second\n')
        self.assertIn(b'"first/shared_secret"',self.call().stderr)
        home_config.unlink()
        self.assertIn(b'"second/shared_secret"',self.call().stderr)

    def test_profiles_are_independent(self):
        path=self.config('shared:\n  pueue_directory: base-data\nprofiles:\n  empty: {}\n  work:\n    shared:\n      pueue_directory: profile-data\n')
        self.assertIn(b'base-data/shared_secret',self.call('-c',path).stderr)
        self.assertIn(str(self.base/'data/pueue/shared_secret').encode(),self.call('-c',path,'-p','empty').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'profile-data/shared_secret',self.call('-c',path,'-p','work').stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'Couldn\'t find profile with name "absent"',self.call('-c',path,'-p','absent').stderr)

    def test_yaml_validation(self):
        path=self.config('shared:\n  use_unix_socket: "yes"\n')
        self.assertIn(b'shared.use_unix_socket: invalid type: string "yes", expected a boolean at line 2 column 20',self.call('-c',path).stderr)
        path=self.config('client: {}\nclient: {}\n')
        self.assertIn(b'duplicate field `client`',self.call('-c',path).stderr)
        path=self.config('shared:\n  use_unix_socket: [\n')
        self.assertIn(b'invalid type: sequence, expected a boolean',self.call('-c',path).stderr)
        path=self.config('profiles:\ndaemon:\n  env_vars: {unset_me: null}\n')
        self.assertNotIn(b'Failed to read configuration.',self.call('-c',path).stderr)

    def test_unix_connection_error(self):
        secret=self.base/'secret'
        secret.write_bytes(b'example secret')
        socket=self.base/'missing.socket'
        path=self.config(f'shared:\n  shared_secret_path: {secret}\n  unix_socket_path: {socket}\n')
        result=self.call('-c',path,'status')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(b'Failed to initialize client.',result.stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'while connecting to daemon. Did you start it?',result.stderr)
        self.assertIn(str(socket).encode(),result.stderr)

    def test_color_controls(self):
        p=self.call('remove','bad',env={'CLICOLOR_FORCE':'1'})
        self.assertTrue(p.stderr.startswith(b'\x1b[1m\x1b[31merror:'))
        p=self.call('remove','bad',env={'CLICOLOR_FORCE':'1','NO_COLOR':'1'})
        self.assertNotIn(b'\x1b',p.stderr)
        p=self.call('--color','always','--help')
        self.assertNotIn(b'\x1b',p.stdout)
        # Runtime diagnostic rendering is independent of the table-color policy.
        self.assertIn(b'\x1b[91m',self.assertNoConfig('--color','never').stderr)

    def test_completion_files(self):
        names={'bash':'pueue.bash','elvish':'pueue.elv','fish':'pueue.fish',
               'power-shell':'_pueue.ps1','zsh':'_pueue','nushell':'pueue.nu'}
        for shell,filename in names.items():
            with self.subTest(shell=shell):
                p=self.call('completions',shell)
                self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stderr),(0,b''))
                self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256(p.stdout).hexdigest(),COMPLETION_HASHES[shell])
                dest=self.base/shell
                dest.mkdir()
                q=self.call('completions',shell,str(dest))
                self.assertEqual((q.returncode,q.stdout,q.stderr),(0,b'',b''))
                self.assertEqual((dest/filename).read_bytes(),p.stdout)
        p=self.call('completions','bash',str(self.base/'missing/destination'))
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(b'Failed to generate completions for Bash',p.stderr)


# Golden digests of the shell completion text observed through the CLI.

if __name__=='__main__':
    unittest.main()

The build uses Python 3's standard library only. It creates a self-contained

## Source organization

- `app/model.py` describes the commands, options, and positional arguments.
- `app/cli.py` handles parsing, typed values, conflicts, and suggestions.
- `app/help_render.py`, `app/help_text.py`, and `app/styling.py` implement the
  reference text, wrapping, and terminal styles.
- `app/completion.py` generates completion scripts for all six supported shells
  from the common command model.
- `app/yaml_reader.py` and `app/configuration.py` implement configuration parsing,
  search-path precedence, independent profiles, and default paths.
- `app/runtime.py` and `app/wire_value.py` implement output-file handling and the
  client connection/diagnostic interface.

The implementation was developed from command-line observations and the bundled
user documentation. The regression tests run the newly built executable without
requiring a daemon, network access, or the observation executable.

Build products, interpreter caches, and local observation files are ignored by
Git. The executable is regenerated entirely from the source files above.
